item.title: [infoq] AI Agent 正在改写 CPU 的价值：当 Token 变成行动，算力竞争不再只是拼 GPU
item.description: Arm's cloud AI solutions architecture director Ravi Malhotra argues that in agentic workloads, CPU performance should no longer be judged mainly by token generation. The CPU has to turn generated tokens into actions such as compiling and testing code, calling tools, hitting databases and isolating sandboxes, while accelerators handle planning. Arm has published an evaluation method covering tool calls, orchestration and end-to-end task execution, developed with Fujitsu, Meta, OpenAI and others.

item.description: FlagOS 2.2 now bundles nine operator libraries covering 1,454 operators, 890 more than the previous release, and reports roughly 27% overall cross-chip performance gains measured across 10 heterogeneous AI chips and over a thousand operators. In one deployment with GLM-5.3-Flash, existing Ascend 910B hardware served 2.04x its previous logical throughput, with rent-equivalent compute cost running 19.4%–27.6% below comparable commercial API pricing.

item.title: [infoq] PostgreSQL 19 发不出来？AI“找茬”太快，人类修Bug的速度跟不上了
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 slipped from October 29 to November 19, with an extra RC2 on November 12, after roughly 8 to 10 significant features were reverted during beta. Core committer and EDB vice president Peter Eisentraut says the cause is not vibe coding but maturing LLM-assisted code review and fuzzing, which surfaced long-tail defects that would otherwise have trickled in over five years. AI raised the effective quality bar faster than humans can fix bugs.

item.title: [v2ex] [OpenAI] 学术写作场景，有啥能优化的吗
item.description: A V2EX poster is asking for help tuning LLM workflows for academic writing over a fixed literature corpus: the model keeps cutting corners when tracing back to source material, and de-AI-flavor tools like Humanizer haven't helped much. They want to know whether a knowledge-graph add-on such as graphify improves retrieval, and what beyond AGENTS.md and skill settings can raise quality. They currently run 6.1 Sol High and haven't compared Claude, Grok or Deepseek yet.

item.title: [infoq] 奥特曼最新 45 分钟访谈：一年不写代码、压力大到不想起床，还嫌 ChatGPT 太谄媚
item.description: In a 45-minute interview with AI blogger Matthew Berman, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he hasn't looked at a line of code in about a year and expects AI to surface candidate treatments for major diseases within a few years. He argued programmers aren't losing jobs to AI but are busier and earning more, and put his GPU demand at effectively unlimited. The conversation also covered AI consciousness, loss-of-control risk, and the pressure that sometimes keeps him in bed.

item.title: [infoq] 决策模型也有专用推理引擎了：StartLux 开源 Prism，单卡最高提速 5.3 倍
item.description: StartLux has open-sourced Prism, an inference engine built specifically for its StartLux-Decision model. On a single NVIDIA H200 running the 27B model, it claims 1.2x to 5.3x the speed of vLLM, cutting a three-question task on one document from 92.9ms to 17.4ms. Because decision models only score a handful of candidate options rather than generate full text, Prism skips whole-vocabulary output and returns bit-identical results regardless of batching; accuracy was 92.94% against 92.97% in BF16.

item.title: [hackernews] Eight Bits of Trust: eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
item.description: Scott Helme recovered the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates straight from their public certificates in under a second, because the keys were tiny integers such as 4, 56 and 115. The compromise was reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on 17 October; Chrome shipped a CRLSet block that evening and Firefox followed hours later through OneCRL.

item.title: [juejin] 一个人+AI做情侣食谱小程序，30天纯赚
item.description: A solo developer built a couples' recipe mini-program with AI as the co-pilot and shares the revenue from its first 30 days online, following up on an earlier post about making just 8 yuan in a month. It offers real backend numbers and a one-person-plus-AI workflow for indie developers curious how cheap a small side project can be.

item.title: [juejin] 基于 Pi，我居然自己搞了一个好用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台
item.description: A Juejin post describes how the author built an AI Agent desktop workbench on top of Pi. Its main argument is not to reinvent the wheel: the model calls, message loop, tool protocol and permission system do not need to be written from scratch. It is aimed at developers who want their own agent desktop tool without rebuilding the plumbing first.

item.title: [github_trending] coollabsio/coolify
item.description: Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable PaaS positioned as an alternative to Vercel, Heroku and Netlify, deploying static sites, databases, full-stack apps and 360-plus one-click services. Any server reachable over SSH works, whether a VPS, bare metal or a Raspberry Pi, so teams keep control of their infrastructure without hand-rolling deployment pipelines.

item.title: [github_trending] AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
item.description: claude-seo is a free, MIT-licensed SEO audit plugin from developer Agrici Daniel that runs inside Claude Code as 26 sub-skills and 19 specialist agents, covering technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, Schema.org markup, E-E-A-T and GEO/AEO for AI search. It also audits agent readiness through Lighthouse Agentic Browsing, WebMCP and llms.txt checks. That mix suits developers who want both Google rankings and citations from ChatGPT, Perplexity and similar engines.

item.title: [juejin] 甲方只给了一张卫星截图，我用 Three.js + Blender 建了一座 3D 能源站
item.description: Starting from a single satellite screenshot handed over by a client, the author rebuilt a 3D integrated energy station with Three.js and Blender: reverse-engineering the design camera from the image, scripting the modeling, baking a night scene in Cycles, then adding a truck reversing into a bay and an operations simulation, with a pixel-by-pixel overlay to check fidelity. Useful for front-end developers working on Web 3D visualization, digital twins, or reconstructing scenes from reference imag

item.title: [juejin] AI 都会写代码了，还要不要学传统编程了? （强烈建议阅读）
item.description: Writing on 掘金, author 狂师 splits programming skill in the AI era into two tracks: non-technical people need to "use" — grasp basic concepts, state requirements clearly and do light acceptance checks — while engineers need to "judge", keeping syntax fundamentals but shifting focus to reading AI-generated code and assessing its quality and risk. His claim is simple: let AI write, keep the responsibility human.

item.title: [juejin] 用了一个月 WorkBuddy，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A heavy GPT user of more than two years, who writes proposals, edits copy and sorts materials with it, explains that he has long relied on third-party relay APIs because of network constraints, and now shares what a month of using WorkBuddy actually felt like. Devs who also reach models through relay endpoints will find this kind of long-term, hands-on account more useful than launch-day benchmarks.

item.title: [36kr] 中国公司全球化周报｜迪拜机场自贸区2026北京交流会报名开启中 / 速卖通与YouTube达成全球战略合作
item.description: This is 36Kr's weekly roundup on Chinese companies expanding overseas, and it carries two items: registration is open for a 2026 Beijing exchange session held by Dubai Airports Free Zone, and AliExpress has signed a global strategic partnership with YouTube. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available. Worth following for teams weighing Middle East expansion or cross-border e-commerce traffic channels.

item.title: [juejin] 太猛了，一个月干到15W+，给大家推荐一个最近爆火的开源逆向工具：REA
item.description: REA is an open-source reverse engineering tool whose repository was only created this April, yet it has climbed past 150,000 stars in little more than a month. The article walks through what the project is and how to get started with it. Useful for anyone doing reverse engineering, security analysis, or binary inspection who wants a quick orientation before trying it out.
